html:
An unequal treaty forced on Joseon Korea by Japan in February 1876, which opened Korea to foreign trade.

For centuries Korea had dealt mainly with China, as a tributary, and kept other foreigners out. The regent Heungseon Daewongun had fought off French and American raids in 1866 and 1871. By 1873 he had lost power to the court of King Gojong. In 1875 a Japanese warship, the Un'yō, provoked a clash at Ganghwa Island near Seoul, and Japan sent a fleet to demand a treaty, much as Perry had done to Japan two decades before.

The treaty declared Korea an independent state, meant to cut its tie to China. It opened Busan and two more ports, let Japan survey the coast, and gave Japanese in Korea the right to be tried by their own consuls. Treaties with the United States and European powers followed in the 1880s. Rivalry over Korea led to Japan's wars with China in 1894 and Russia in 1904, and to Japan's annexation of Korea in 1910.
sum: An unequal treaty forced on Joseon Korea by Japan in February 1876, which opened Korea to foreign trade.
